name: lodash-functions-in-restify-validation
behavioral_change: lodash 4.0.0 narrowed `_.functions` to return only an object's own method names, excluding inherited ones; the same release also removed the `thisArg` parameter from iteration methods (a third argument to `_.reduce` is silently ignored) and removed the alias `_.contains` in favor of `_.includes`. The dominant change is the `_.functions` narrowing; its name and signature are unchanged.
downstream_effect: The downstream project (restify-validation) builds its validator table with `_.functions(validator)` on an object created by `Object.create`, so after the upgrade only 3 of 54 validators are registered and rules such as `isEmail` silently pass. The failures are should assertions such as `expected 0 to be 1` in `test/units/validators_test.js` and `test/units/validation_test.js` with frames inside should; lodash, `_.functions` and the prototype chain are never mentioned.
reference_fix: The reference fix edits three production sites: `_.functions(validator)` to `_.functionsIn(validator)` at `lib/validators.js:152`, `_.reduce(coll, fn, false, this)` to `_.reduce(coll, fn.bind(this), false)` at `lib/validators.js:104`, and `_.contains` to `_.includes` at `lib/conditions.js:31`.
documented_in: The lodash Changelog v4.0.0 (https://github.com/lodash/lodash/wiki/Changelog#v400): Compatibility Warnings states that `_.functions` returns only own method names and that `thisArg` params were removed (that entry includes before and after code), and Notable Changes, Removed 17 aliases, states `_.contains` was removed in favor of `_.includes`. Tier 2 by the dominant component: the `_.functions` entry is prose only and `_.functionsIn` is derived from the API reference.
